entries.definition: An ICBM that enters a low-altitude orbit before reentering to strike its target, with much shorter flight times if flying the same direction as traditional ICBMs

A maneuverable aerodynamic body that is typically delivered by a ballistic missile, achieves sustained hypersonic glide at altitudes of 15-50 km, and glides for at least half of its flight to its target. HGVs can be armed with a nuclear warhead.
A ground-based missile with a range exceeding 5,500 km that flies on a ballistic trajectory
A ground-based ballistic missile with a range between between 3,000–5,500 km
A ground-based ballistic missile with a range between between 1,000–3,000 km
A formation of Russia’s Strategic Rocket Forces, subordinate to a missile army, that groups several missile regiments. Russia’s ICBM force has 12 divisions across three missile armies.
A ballistic missile loaded with several warheads, each of which can be aimed at different target or to the same target in different time intervals
The basic firing unit of a Russian missile division, operating a group of roughly six to ten ICBM launchers, either in silos controlled from a launch control center or on road-mobile vehicles.

The military of the People’s Republic of China, which serves the ruling Communist Party of China. It is made up of four services (the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Rocket Force) and four service arms (the Aerospace Force, Cyberspace Force, Information Support Force, and Joint Logistics Support Force)

The People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force is the element of the Chinese military responsible for organizing, manning, training, and equipping the strategic land-based nuclear and tactical missile forces as well as their supporting elements and bases.
A missile interceptor placed in orbit that is designed to destroy missiles during their boost phase, the first few minutes of flight while the engines are still burning
A ballistic missile, typically carrying nuclear warheads, launched from a submarine
A rocket used to carry a payload from Earth into outer space. It requires a clear understanding of many of the same technologies used in the development of long-range ballistic missiles
A trailer-based launch system in which a separate tractor or prime mover tows the trailer, which raises and launches the missile
An integrated vehicle that transports a missile, raises it into its launch position, and launches it
A ground-based ballistic missile with a range of less than 1,000 km

entries.term: Ship Submersible Ballistic Nuclear (Ballistic Missile Submarine)
entries.definition: A nuclear-powered submarine armed with submarine-launched ballistic missiles carrying multiple nuclear warheads. It forms the sea-based leg of the nuclear triad and is the most survivable of the three legs.
Nuclear weapons that are delivered by shorter-range systems and carry lower-yield warheads, intended for use against troops or facilities on the battlefield
China’s term for a launch-on-warning posture, in which a retaliatory launch is authorized once an adversary’s missiles are confirmed in flight but before impact.
A group of missiles launched simultaneously or in rapid succession as part of a single attack
A nuclear strategy built on being able to survive a first strike in order to retaliate and cause unacceptable damage to the adversary
A nuclear strike aimed at an adversary’s military forces, installations, and assets, as opposed to its population
A nuclear strike aimed at an adversary’s cities, population, and economy.

The basic combat unit of the People's Liberation Army Rocket Force, made up of 4-6 launch battalions. The force consists of nuclear missile forces, conventional missile forces, and combat support forces

A heavily defended sea area where one’s own naval forces can operate with relative safety. Such an area is typically enclosed by friendly or allied coastlines, incorporates defensive infrastructure, and is subject to intensive patrols by national forces

A nuclear force structure made up of three types of long-range delivery systems, also known as legs: land-based ICBMs, submarine-launched ballistic missiles on ballistic missile submarines, and heavy bombers. It is designed so that no single attack or technical failure can eliminate a country’s ability to retaliate

A Russian silo-based, liquid-fueled heavy ICBM designed to replace the RS-20V Voevoda. It is believed to be capable of delivering up to 10 nuclear warheads an to have an operational range of over 35,000 km
A Soviet-era, silo-based heavy ICBM, first deployed in 1988, that was declared under arms control treaties as carrying 10 warheads.
An experimental North Korean road-mobile ICBM that was never flight-tested and never deployed, and analysts remain uncertain whether it was ever an operational weapons program
North Korea’s first ICBM to fly, first tested on July 4, 2017, and a direct evolution of the single-stage Hwasong-12 intermediate-range missile. Analysts estimate its range to be roughly 10,400 km
A larger North Korean ICBM, first flight-tested on November 28, 2017, with greater technical characteristics than the Hwasong-14. Its estimated range is about 13,000 km.
The amount of time between target missile launch and plume detection by a space-based infrared sensing constellation
The maximum speed of the interceptor. This occurs exactly as the interceptor engine burns the last of its fuel in an idealized, 2-phase flyout ranging model.

The number of unique interceptors hosted on a single satellite in the larger space-based interceptor constellation. Previously, the number of space-based interceptors was assumed equal to the number of satellites.
In this tool, salvo size refers to the number of offensive missiles launched simultaneously from any one target point
The amount of time between plume detection by a space-based infrared sensing constellation and the actual release of the space-based interceptor from its host satellite.
